title: Best Podcast Cover Art Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a podcast cover art designer: size requirements, readability, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags.
intro: Podcast cover art is what people see in podcast apps, usually as a small square next to many other shows. It needs to show your topic and style instantly and stay readable when tiny. Covers go wrong when the title is too small, the design is cluttered, or the file does not meet the podcast platforms' size rules. This guide helps you get cover art that stands out in a crowded list.

faq.q: What size does podcast cover art need?
faq.a: Podcast platforms ask for a square image within a specific pixel range and file size. Check your hosting platform and major podcast apps for current requirements and share them with the designer.

faq.q: How much text should the cover have?
faq.a: Usually just the show name, and perhaps the host's name. Long subtitles become unreadable at small sizes.

faq.q: Should my photo be on the cover?
faq.a: It can help for personality-driven shows. For topic-based shows, a strong visual symbol may work better.

faq.q: Can I get episode graphics too?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for templates for episode artwork and social posts in the same style.

faq.q: What makes cover art get rejected?
faq.a: Wrong size, low resolution, misleading content or unauthorized use of logos or images. Follow the platforms' guidelines.
